day_shape: 74 items: 26-nation UK-led Strait of Hormuz coalition statement, Trump posts Iran 'decimation to be continued' after Xi summit, CENTCOM says Iran defence industry set back 90%, Hezbollah kills IDF soldier in south Lebanon, four UK parliamentary questions tabled on Iran.

threads.label: Trump-Xi summit and Iran fallout
threads.summary: Trump posted that 'military decimation of Iran' is 'to be continued' after discussing Hormuz with Xi Jinping in Beijing, and told Fox News he would not be 'much more patient' with Tehran. China's Foreign Ministry said using force on Iran's nuclear issue has reached a 'dead end', and Iran International assessed Xi may help on Iran but at a price.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz coalition and shipping
threads.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence published a 26-nation joint statement on the Multinational Military Mission for the Strait of Hormuz, signed by France, Germany, Japan, Korea, Bahrain, Qatar and others. Times of Israel reported a ship seized and diverted to Iran and another sunk in the strait, while an Iranian lawmaker called for annual fees on fibre-optic cables crossing Hormuz.

threads.label: CENTCOM and US damage assessments
threads.summary: CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said US bombings reduced Iran's defence industry by 90% though Tehran could still strike, per Jerusalem Post and Times of Israel. IRIB cited Senators Chris Murphy and Tammy Duckworth saying Iran retains most missiles and drones and that Trump's stated war goals remain unrealised.

threads.label: Hezbollah-Israel border exchanges
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported an IDF soldier killed by a Hezbollah mortar shell in south Lebanon and three civilians hurt in a Hezbollah attack on northern Israel ahead of a third round of Israel-Lebanon talks. Defa Press claimed Hezbollah targeted Israeli forces in multiple operations, and the IDF told ToI the Hezbollah drone threat was serious but overstated.

threads.label: BRICS diplomacy in New Delhi
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi addressed BRICS foreign ministers in New Delhi calling for UN reform and against 'economic terrorism', and met India's and South Africa's foreign ministers. Iran International reported Araghchi accused the UAE of direct involvement in military operations against Iran during the meeting.

threads.label: UN humanitarian reporting and Yemen deal
threads.summary: UN OCHA's ReliefWeb published a tenth-week Middle East mobility report and a WHO situation report noting Iran-Lebanon ceasefires holding but fragile, with continued hostilities in southern Lebanon. The UN Secretary-General's spokesperson announced Yemeni parties agreed in Amman to release over 1,600 conflict-related detainees, the largest such deal of the war.

threads.label: UK Parliament Iran questions tabled
threads.summary: Four parliamentary questions on Iran were tabled, covering Baha'i persecution (James Naish), the detention of Lindsay and Craig Foreman (Susan Murray), fuel-cost impacts linked to Iran developments (Dame Caroline Dinenage), and Iran's nomination to the UN Committee for Program and Coordination (Lord Goldsmith). The FCDO also updated its list of Iran designations and sanctions notices.

events.title_en: Chain of Trump's humiliation by Iran and China
events.summary_en: Chain of Trump's humiliation by Iran and China. Robert Pape, University of Chicago professor: Xi Jinping is humiliating Trump and trying to reverse the narrative only makes things worse. First, Iranian negotiators refused to meet with Trump's envoys. Then Friedrich Merz, Chancellor of Germany, openly said that Trump is being humiliated. Then Saudi Arabia began distancing itself from Trump. Trump is now facing a major crisis similar to the crisis of Lyndon Johnson (US President in the 1960s who was weakened by political pressures, both domestic and foreign, particularly the Vietnam War).

events.title_en: China: Using force against Iran is a 'dead end'
events.summary_en: China: Using force against Iran is a 'dead end'. Spokesman of China's Foreign Ministry said: The confrontation between Iran and the United States should never have occurred from the start and there is no need for it to continue. Finding a solution as soon as possible is in the interest of the United States, Iran, countries of the region and the world. Reaching an agreement on Iran's nuclear file is essential, and the use of force will be a dead end. We will continue to cooperate with the international community to provide stronger support for negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

events.title_en: China: On Iran's nuclear issue, using force has reached a dead end
events.summary_en: China: On Iran's nuclear issue, using force has reached a dead end. China's Foreign Ministry: Using force on Iran's nuclear issue has reached a dead end and military solutions are not the answer. The confrontation between Iran and America should never have happened, there is no need for it to continue, and Beijing has always believed that dialogue and negotiation is the best way, and a quick solution must be found. China's Foreign Ministry called for a comprehensive and permanent ceasefire and emphasised that reaching a swift solution to end this crisis will be in everyone's interest, and Beijing will continue cooperating with the international community to provide stronger support for peace talks between Iran and Washington.

events.summary_en: Araghchi: Iran seeks serious reform of the UN structure. The Foreign Minister on the second day of the meeting of Foreign Ministers of BRICS member states: Today, sanctions have become a weapon that destroys people's basic rights. events.title_en: Araghchi: BRICS countries view Iran differently after America's failed aggression
events.summary_en: Araghchi: BRICS countries view Iran differently after America's failed aggression. The common thread of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the BRICS summit is the current situation and the illegal aggression against Iran. All countries are eager to know how Iran was able to emerge from the recent war victorious and with honour, and of course the developments that may occur in the future. All countries present acknowledge that Iran was victorious in the recent war and Iran's enemies have failed in achieving their objectives. With the end of the war, Iran is viewed from a different perspective.

events.title_en: Senator Murphy: Iran is far more powerful today than at the start of the war
events.summary_en: Senator Murphy: Iran is far more powerful today than at the start of the war. War with Iran is not a stalemate; it is a disaster for America. Intelligence reports show they still possess the majority of their missiles and drones. They have also maintained their nuclear programme and can resume military operations in the Strait of Hormuz whenever they wish. The best path forward is for Trump to end the blockade right now and declare the end of the war, and hope that other countries can use effective diplomacy to pave the way for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
